title: Contract negotiation quick reference for inference operators
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact negotiation cheat-sheet for commercial teams and security reviewers when contracting external inference providers or onboarding managed inference partners. Focus is on inference-specific risks (ephemeral caches, KV storage, model weights, residual outputs) and practical fallbacks/SLAs used in negotiations.

Top negotiation priorities (one-liners):
- Data residency & segmentation: be explicit about which data classes may leave your tenant or region and require per-customer logical segregation for regulated customers.
- Ephemeral data guarantees: insist on bounded retention for caches/kv and cryptographic deletion proofs or deletion timelines.
- Incident response & forensics: defined timelines for notification, evidence preservation, and access to logs for customer audits.
- Model provenance & weight handling: limits on exporting model weights, controls for fine-tuning, and IP indemnities.
- Availability SLAs and credits tied to inference latency and successful request percentage (p95/p99).
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: contractual right to automatic fallback to alternate model variants and documented behavior during capacity loss.
- Escrow & escrow-like remedies for air-gapped/on-prem deployments.

Checklist for legal + security reviewers (quick pass):
1) Data handling and retention rules
   - Does the contract specify retention windows for inference logs, prefixes, and KV cache entries? (target: <= 30 days unless otherwise approved)
   - Are there per-environment retention differing for prod vs. staging?
   - Clear exceptions for ephemeral debugging snapshots and emergency forensics with approval process

2) Access & segregation controls
   - Customer isolation: dedicated namespaces, tenant-aware routing, or dedicated pools for high-risk customers
   - Admin & operator access logging and MFA for privileged access to tenant data

3) Encryption & key management
   - In-transit TLS and at-rest encryption for stored artifacts
   - Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) option for private deployments
   - Key rotation obligations and disclosure requirements if keys are rotated by vendor

4) Audit rights & evidence
   - Right to on-site or remote evidence collection with notice windows (e.g., 30 days)
   - Required audit evidence: access logs, KV deletion proofs, container images and signatures for on-prem.

5) Incident response and timeline commitments
   - Notification: initial notice within 24 hours of detection, preliminary report within 48–72 hours, and full RCA within 30 days
   - Remediation commitments and SLA credits tied to incident severity

6) Service levels relevant to inference
   - Availability expressed as successful inference request rate (e.g., >= 99.9% monthly) and/or p99 latency thresholds per model class
   - Token-level success criteria for streaming APIs (e.g., streaming connections not to exceed X% failure)
   - Clear definitions of force majeure and carrier events vs. vendor responsibility for capacity failures

7) Model handling, weights and export controls
   - Prohibit export of model weights unless expressly permitted; require secure transfer procedures and NDA for weight sharing
   - Restrictions on vendor controlling the customer’s derived models or fine-tuning unless customer consents
   - Export-control and sanctioned-entity compliance warranties

8) Limitation of liability and indemnities
   - Carveouts for security breach costs and customer regulatory fines may be negotiated separately
   - Consider aggregator liability caps plus mutual indemnities for third-party IP claims tied to vendor-provided model weights

9) Termination & transition assistance
   - Transition data export format and schedule (e.g., standard JSON lines and TTL for caches)
   - Contractual obligation for ephemeral data purge and certification of deletion within a timeframe (e.g., 30–60 days)

10) Pricing and cost controls
   - Token meter transparency (unit definitions) and overage policies
   - Mechanism for emergency capacity or burst pricing and rights to switch to alternate routing to control cost

Sample clause snippets (drop-in edits):
- Ephemeral KV/cache retention (sample):
  "Vendor shall retain ephemeral inference caches (including prefix caches and KV state derived from customer requests) for no longer than thirty (30) calendar days unless Customer provides written instruction otherwise. Upon Customer's request, Vendor will provide a signed attestation of secure deletion within ten (10) business days and reasonable supporting logs demonstrating deletion operations."

- Incident notification & evidence (sample):
  "Vendor will provide Customer with initial notification of any security incident affecting Customer data within twenty-four (24) hours of Vendor's detection. Vendor will: (a) provide a preliminary incident report within seventy-two (72) hours, (b) preserve all forensic evidence for not less than ninety (90) days, and (c) permit Customer or its designated auditor reasonable access to relevant logs and artifacts for the purposes of investigation, subject to confidentiality obligations."

- SLA and credits (sample):
  "Vendor warrants that the Service will process successful inference requests at a monthly availability of at least 99.9% measured as the percentage of HTTP/2 completion responses within the agreed latency objective. For any monthly period in which availability falls below the warranty, Customer is entitled to a service credit equal to 5% of monthly fees for each 0.1% below warranty, up to 50% of that month's fees."

- Model export / weights (sample):
  "Vendor shall not distribute, transfer, or otherwise make available to any third party Customer-specific model weights, checkpoints, or derivations derived from Customer data without Customer's prior written consent. Vendor will maintain an auditable record of all exports and will implement technical controls to block unauthorized exports for Hosted and Dedicated deployments."

Negotiation playbook (practical):
- Commercial kickoff: Align on three priorities with the counterparty: (1) retention bounds, (2) SLA/latency baseline, (3) operator access controls. Get an initial term-sheet with these bullets before legal exchange.
- Security wishlist (non-negotiables): on-demand key isolation, deletion certification window <= 30 days, 24h incident notification.
- Concession ladder (what to give up first): burst pricing protections, small increases to retention for debugging (e.g., push from 30 to 60 days with logging and approvals), non-prod retention exemptions.
- Escalation triggers: require CISO-to-CISO call if there is any divergence on forensic access, key management, or weight-exporting clauses.

Fallbacks and operational playbooks to attach to contract:
- Auto-routing fallback: define a contractual policy that on model pool capacity breach, requests will be routed to the next-compatible model tier (e.g., lower-precision or quantized variant) with documented delta in cost and expected quality.
- Emergency sequester: vendor agrees to immediate isolating of impacted customer data pools and coordinated snapshot for forensic review upon suspected compromise.
- Rollback & rollback evidence: vendor must preserve prior 30 days of model-serving images and config to support rollback attempts for a period of 90 days after an incident.

Red flags to escalate to legal/security leadership:
- Vendor refuses deletion attestation or won’t provide a timeline for ephemeral cache purging.
- Vendor disclaims forensic access entirely or says only internal investigators can view logs.
- Vendor demands broad indemnity from customer for third-party model IP issues while refusing constraints on weight export.

Negotiation examples and suggested trade-offs:
- If vendor insists on longer cache retention for debugging (e.g., 90 days), require: (a) strict scoped access logs, (b) encryption with customer-managed keys, and (c) quarterly deletion attestation.
- If vendor resists SLA credit formulas, accept a capped ramp of credits for the first 3 months of the pilot and tighten for annual renewals.

Appendix: evidence buckets to ask for in onboarding
- Artifact list: access logs, operator action logs, KV purge logs, container image signatures, KMS access records, model export audit trail.
- Minimum formats: CSV/JSON time-series for logs with UTC timestamps and consistent request IDs.
- Retention matrix: mapping of artifact -> contractual retention (e.g., request logs 90 days, KV purge proofs 365 days).

Notes and open questions (internal):
- Evaluate whether we want to add a standard 'ephemeral-kv-scrub proof' mechanism (HMAC over deletion time + request id) for high-risk customers.
- Check compatibility of proposed SLA metrics with telemetry available from hosted runtime (p99 latency per model family is currently feasible; token-level success metrics need infra instrumentation).

Summary: keep it tight, prioritize deletion/forensics/SLAs. Use the auto-routing fallback language to avoid planned downtime impacting end-users. Keep an evidence checklist attached to the contract so onboarding can validate quickly.

Author notes: drafted for legal + product pairing during commercial negotiation. Use as a living document and attach specific clause text to the master contract as exhibits when agreed.
